text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Mubarak and Chancellor Helmut Kohl to discuss today in Germany joint Egyptian and European cooperation and the developments in the peace process. Mubarak tells German newspaper that his talks with Kohl will include clarifying the reasons behind the deadlocked peace process. Mubarak says that a comprehensive peace is not possible without reaching an agreement with Syria.
- In August, the second tranche of compensation for damages in the Gulf war will be paid to 54,000 beneficiaries in Egypt.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri will inspect the new metro project fron Ramses to Tahrir.
- 28 factories are held responsible and referred to the public prosecutor for polluting the Nile and threatening public health.
- Rice farmers will be exempt from fees for the 1995/96 season.
- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid said that there are studies underway on privatising drinking water stations.
- Mubarak and the President of Djibouti Hassan Gouled discuss bilateral ties and the situation in Somalia.
- Mubarak says during his visit to Germany that Israel will be the loser if the peace process collapses, and there is a need to stick to the Oslo agreement.
